steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

        """Extract traceback information.

        Args:
            exc_type (Type[BaseException]): Exception type.
            exc_value (BaseException): Exception value.
            traceback (TracebackType): Python Traceback object.
            show_locals (bool, optional): Enable display of local variables. Defaults to False.
            locals_max_length (int, optional): Maximum length of containers before abbreviating, or None for no abbreviation.
                Defaults to 10.
            locals_max_string (int, optional): Maximum length of string before truncating, or None to disable. Defaults to 80.
            locals_hide_dunder (bool, optional): Hide locals prefixed with double underscore. Defaults to True.
            locals_hide_sunder (bool, optional): Hide locals prefixed with single underscore. Defaults to False.

        Returns:
            Trace: A Trace instance which you can use to construct a `Traceback`.
        """

        stacks: List[Stack] = []
        is_cause = False

        from rich import _IMPORT_CWD

        def safe_str(_object: Any) -> str:
            """Don't allow exceptions from __str__ to propagate."""
            try:
                return str(_object)
            except Exception:
                return "<exception str() failed>"

        while True:
            stack = Stack(
                exc_type=safe_str(exc_type.__name__),
                exc_value=safe_str(exc_value),
                is_cause=is_cause,
            )

            if isinstance(exc_value, SyntaxError):
                stack.syntax_error = _SyntaxError(
                    offset=exc_value.offset or 0,
                    filename=exc_value.filename or "?",
                    lineno=exc_value.lineno or 0,
                    line=exc_value.text or "",
                    msg=exc_value.msg,
                )

            stacks.append(stack)
            append = stack.frames.append

            def get_locals(
                iter_locals: Iterable[Tuple[str, object]]
            ) -> Iterable[Tuple[str, object]]:
                """Extract locals from an iterator of key pairs."""
                if not (locals_hide_dunder or locals_hide_sunder):
                    yield from iter_locals
                    return
                for key, value in iter_locals:
                    if locals_hide_dunder and key.startswith("__"):
                        continue
                    if locals_hide_sunder and key.startswith("_"):
                        continue
                    yield key, value

            for frame_summary, line_no in walk_tb(traceback):
                filename = frame_summary.f_code.co_filename
                if filename and not filename.startswith("<"):
                    if not os.path.isabs(filename):
                        filename = os.path.join(_IMPORT_CWD, filename)
                if frame_summary.f_locals.get("_rich_traceback_omit", False):
                    continue

                frame = Frame(
                    filename=filename or "?",
                    lineno=line_no,
                    name=frame_summary.f_code.co_name,
                    locals={
                        key: pretty.traverse(
                            value,
                            max_length=locals_max_length,
                            max_string=locals_max_string,
                        )
                        for key, value in get_locals(frame_summary.f_locals.items())
                    }
                    if show_locals
                    else None,
                )
                append(frame)
                if frame_summary.f_locals.get("_rich_traceback_guard", False):
                    del stack.frames[:]

            cause = getattr(exc_value, "__cause__", None)
            if cause:
                exc_type = cause.__class__
                exc_value = cause
                # __traceback__ can be None, e.g. for exceptions raised by the
                # 'multiprocessing' module
                traceback = cause.__traceback__
                is_cause = True
                continue

            cause = exc_value.__context__
            if cause and not getattr(exc_value, "__suppress_context__", False):
                exc_type = cause.__class__
                exc_value = cause
                traceback = cause.__traceback__
                is_cause = False
                continue
            # No cover, code is reached but coverage doesn't recognize it.
            break  # pragma: no cover

        trace = Trace(stacks=stacks)
        return trace
